features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures hands-on experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, hardening, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or advanced degree preparation the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing agent-based systems with bounded autonomy, supervision, permissions, guardrails, or supporting backend infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or autonomous tooling experience is described.
Mentions agents or automation in broad terms, but without architecture detail.
Describes building agent pipelines or systems end to end.
Shows principled agent architecture, such as bounded tasks, permissions, auditing, or explicit Go/Python control separation.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter provides credible, concrete evidence of applied strength with data structures and algorithms.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers through defaults, tooling, lower friction, and embedding secure behavior into normal workflows.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Engineering rigor and maintainability
features.description: Captures emphasis on reliability, correctness, testing, maintainability, failure awareness, and long-term operability of security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter backs claims with concrete technical examples, mechanisms, named systems, or other specific supporting detail.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Formal security credentials
features.description: Captures the presence and strength of formal third-party security certifications or credential signals.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-relevant Go appears in the applicant's backend engineering experience.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter states the concrete outcomes, effects, or measurable results of the applicant's work rather than just activities or responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages the letter presents beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Learning and collaboration posture
features.description: Captures humility, coachability, and willingness to partner with security specialists or internal users rather than presenting the work as purely solo execution.

levels.descriptor: No collaboration signal appears beyond applying for the role.
Cross-functional work is implied, but the posture toward security specialists is not explicit.
The letter explicitly shows enthusiasm for close collaboration with security engineers or learning from specialist teammates.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: Captures whether the letter forms a clear, well-structured story or thesis linking background, motivation, and fit instead of reading like a disconnected list.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like disconnected bullets, fragments, or stacked claims.
The letter has some structure, but transitions or the overall arc are uneven.
The letter coherently links background, technical experience, and interest in the role.
The letter presents an especially well-shaped narrative that makes the applicant's trajectory and fit feel natural.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures how memorable, individualized, and voiceful the letter feels beyond basic correctness and completeness.

levels.descriptor: The letter feels interchangeable, checklist-driven, or heavily templated.
The letter has some personal framing, but is still mostly standard and forgettable.
The letter has a noticeable voice or framing device that helps the applicant stand out.
The letter delivers a vivid, controlled narrative that is both memorable and well matched to the role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing adversarial or attacker-minded security practice outside normal product work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures contribution to, maintenance of, or upstream responsibility for public codebases and software used beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures how technically ambitious, rigorous, and role-relevant the applicant's self-directed projects appear outside day-job work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational platform or infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: No real signal of interest in shared infrastructure or broad downstream impact.
General statements about scale or impact without tying them to platform work.
Explicitly says they prefer foundational or internal tooling work with organization-wide reach.
Frames past choices and future goals around compounding leverage from shared systems across many teams.

features.name: Production ownership breadth
features.description: Captures the breadth and level of responsibility the letter shows for shipped production systems, including launches, maintenance, and ownership across services.

levels.descriptor: Production scope is vague or very limited, with at most one clearly owned service.
The letter shows clear responsibility across about 2 production services.
The letter shows repeated production delivery across about 4 services.
The letter shows broad production breadth across 6 or more services or similarly wide operational scope.

features.name: Professional tenure
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience or time in role the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and credibly the letter shows Python as a substantial production language for services, automation, tooling, or agents.

levels.descriptor: No Python evidence, or Python is only named without context.
Python is mentioned for basic scripting or generic use.
Shows substantial production Python use in services, automation, or internal tooling.
Shows deep production Python use with quality signals such as typed, tested, extensible, or central security tooling.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter connects the applicant's background and motivation to this exact role, team, or set of responsibilities rather than to a generic software job.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures the depth and concreteness of hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues through review, threat modeling, analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands the role's core leverage as scaling security expertise and workflows through principled automation at organizational scale.

levels.descriptor: No broader framing of security automation is given.
Automation is mentioned mainly as convenience or efficiency, without a systems view.
The letter clearly frames automation as reducing toil or scaling team output.
The letter shows strategic understanding of capacity multiplication, centralizing scarce judgment, or variant-analysis-style leverage.

features.name: Security worldview
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful point of view about what security engineering is for and how secure systems should be approached.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinctive security philosophy beyond generic enthusiasm.
Shows broad positive sentiment about security or impact, but little deeper framing.
Expresses a clear philosophy about rigor, resilience, secure defaults, or invisible success.
Offers a memorable, specific philosophy that strongly reinforces fit for this kind of security work.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or handling of vulnerability reports or findings.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general interest in automating security work, but no concrete triage example.
Gives a concrete example of building automation for vulnerability intake or report handling.
Shows clear ownership of triage automation and explains how it reduced manual work or improved flow.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures surface-level mechanical quality, including spelling, grammar, proofreading, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic or composite constructs that do not cleanly match a broader recurring criterion.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors noticeably distract and undermine polish.
Several errors are present, but the letter remains readable.
Only minor errors are present.
The letter is clean and professional throughout.
